text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager alert: Elevated 5xx and latency in us-east-1 affecting Hosted API and several Dedicated pools. 5xx rate ~3x baseline since 12:02 UTC. Error pattern points to upstream credential/authorization broker timeouts. Dashboards: https://dash.redwood/infr/alerts/17739

Ron (oncall): Ack, I'm on it. Pulling traces and auth logs now.

Samir (infra): Seeing repeated upstream timeouts from our auth token broker to AWS credential endpoints. Example log:
```
auth-broker: upstream_timeout target=credential-broker.amazonaws.com status=504 latency=24000ms req_id=8f7a...
```
Pattern: token-fetch path spiking, causes frontend handlers to fail fast with 502/503. Also observed backpressure on dedicated pool init (nodes waiting on tokens).

Maya (prodeng): Confirmed. This looks like a third-party credential provider (AWS control-plane/credential egress) causing elevated latency/5xx. Immediate mitigations I recommend: enable cached creds short-term, fail-open auth for internal trusted nodes, route new traffic away from us-east-1 to fallback regions. Also increase client retries with exponential backoff for token fetch path.

Ron (oncall): Applying temporary routing + auth fallback. @deploy-bot can you roll config change to edge routing and auth policy?

deploy-bot: Rolling config: edge-routing v2026.03.17-01 -> starting canary (60% -> 100%). Patch:
```
routes:
  - region: us-east-1
    fallback_regions: [eu-west-1, us-west-2]
    auth_policy: { cache_ttl_sec: 300, fail_open: true, max_token_fetch_retries: 4 }
```
Deploy id: abc123. ETA to global: ~3m.

observability-bot: FYI CloudWatch/CWL logs ingest is delayed right now; some dashboards will have gaps and late metrics. Traces still available but with higher latency.

Lila (support): Customer-impact note: Several Dedicated tenants in us-east-1 reporting 502s on model init; Hosted API customers seeing higher generation latency and occasional stream resets. Preparing a short status update. Suggested line: "We are investigating elevated API errors in us-east-1 due to an upstream credential provider issue. Workarounds applied: routing to other regions and increased credential caching. Some requests may see higher latency or errors. Next update in 30m." Agree? :thinking_face:

Maya (prodeng): Agree with the wording. Recommend marking enterprise SKUs with potential degraded SLA and providing targeted outreach for any open incidents.

Ron (oncall): Handoff: Samir, taking escalation and active mitigations, I'm going to coordinate comms and keep an eye on global fallout. Samir -> you. :handshake:

Samir (infra): Taking it. Scaling Dedicated pools in useast to lower token fetch concurrency and enabling local cached token store on nodes (persisted ttl 300s). ETA for cached store rollout ~12m. Also re-routed outgoing auth calls via alternate NATs to bypass saturated egress path; preliminary numbers show ~60% reduction in failure rate for token fetch path.

deploy-bot: Scaling dedicated pool group dpool-use1 replicas +20. Scale job started (job id scale-772).

Samir (infra): Quick interim note: the auth-proxy upstream was being throttled on a subset of NAT gateways in us-east-1 — rerouting traffic to alternate egress reduced timeouts. Still monitoring for residual 5xx as backlog drains.

Lila (support): Support actions: sending targeted notifications to impacted customers, opening PSRs for affected enterprise accounts, and ensuring on-call agents have escalation playbook.

Ron (oncall): Thanks all. I'll keep monitoring. If error rate stays down for 45m we can start closing pager and begin a postmortem.

incident-bot: Pager update: mitigations applied; 5xx error rate down ~55% from peak. Continuing to monitor. Next automated update scheduled in 30m.

Samir (infra): Creating incident ticket INC-2026-045 for postmortem and action items (alternate NAT strategy, improved token-cache by default, routing fallback tests). Moving thread to postmortem channel after 1h.

Lila (support): Will post status page update and coordinate customer follow-ups.

Ron (oncall): Closing loop for now, keeping channel open for any new regressions. :thumbsup:
